transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-05-22
Time: 16:30 PDT
Duration: ~42 minutes
Attendees: Carlos Mendez (Redwood AE), Priya Rao (Redwood SE), Maya Singh (Crestwood CTO), James Ortiz (Platform Eng), Lena Park (Security)

Summary: quick product walkthrough focused on rate limiting, quotas, and multi-tenant org/project key controls. Discussed hosted vs dedicated rate enforcement, per-project quotas, burst capacity, and compliance concerns. Agreed to trial org with project keys and follow-up benchmark.

Topics: rate limits, org/project keys, per-route quotas, SSO/roles, KMS/encryption, SOC2, trial setup, benchmarking

Transcript:
[00:00] Carlos: hey everyone, thanks for joining, i'm carlos from redwood - i'll kick things off and priya will do the demo; how are you all doing?
[00:08] Maya: good thanks, yes excited to see the rate limiting and tenant controls, we've been hitting some token spikes in prod.
[00:15] Priya: cool, quick agenda - overview of org vs project keys, how rate limits are enforced at route/model/user levels, demo of console+api and then Q&A.
[00:30] James: perfect - we care about per-tenant quotas, per-route budget, and also the ability to override for particular projects.
[00:40] Priya: totally. so redwood supports org-level limits (global commitment), project-level keys which you can pin to teams, and route-level quotas for endpoints. we'll show the console now.
[00:50] [00:50] Priya shares screen / console loads (brief pause)
[01:05] Priya: here you can see our org dashboard, top right is "rate limits & quotas" - we have applied a committed throughput for the org plus burst tokens that allow short spikes without failing requests.
[01:20] Maya: when you say burst tokens, is that per-org or per-project?
[01:24] Priya: it's per-org by default but you can enable per-project burst allowances. that's useful when one product team needs short-term higher TPS.
[01:36] James: and are quotas token-based or request-based? we usually budget on tokens because models vary a lot.
[01:41] Priya: yes tokens. our UI uses token budget and you can set soft/hard limits per project or per route. the API also exposes headers so your app can surface remaining tokens.
[01:55] Lena: how do you handle enforcement timing - i.e., do you rate limit at edge, or at the runtime? we need guarantees for VPC/private deployments too.
[02:05] Priya: good question. for hosted we enforce at the edge gateway for the org; for dedicated/private we ship an enforcement daemon in the control plane close to the runtime. there's an option for local enforcement inside the VPC so you don't hit public endpoints.
[02:22] Carlos: to add, in private deployments we can integrate with your KMS and RBAC so enforcement and audit logs stay inside your network.
[02:30] [02:30] Priya: demo - creating a project key now; i'll click new project, name = "patient-summaries", assign to team, set monthly token quota = 2,000,000 and set burst = 200k, then save.
[02:48] Priya: now you'll see the key appears and api call examples on right - it shows limit headers: X-Redwood-Quota-Remaining, X-Redwood-Burst-Remaining.
[03:05] James: nice, can we scope keys to models or routes? we have some expensive models we want to isolate.
[03:10] Priya: yes - you can restrict a project key to a model set or to specific routes (e.g., /v1/chat/completions). we also support weight-based quotas if you want models to consume tokens differently.
[03:24] Maya: what's the developer flow for rotating keys? we need automated rotation for security.
[03:28] Priya: keys are managed through the console and API; rotation can be done via our API with key create/disable endpoints. for private deployments you can hook into your secrets manager.
[03:40] [03:40] Carlos: quick qual - what's your timeline and success criteria?
[03:44] Maya: timeline is end of Q3 for a pilot, success = predictable token costs, no noisy tenants exceeding budgets, and security sign-off.
[03:53] Priya: perfect, pilot fits well. we'll give you a trial org with project keys and suggest a benchmark run.
[03:59] James: on benchmarking - can we throttle to simulate worst-case noisy neighbor? we want to see tail latency under heavy batching.
[04:07] Priya: yes, we have a workload generator. for hosted tests we can run against your trial org; for dedicated we'll coordinate capacity. we'll share the benchmark harness repo.
[04:20] Lena: compliance - we need SOC 2 + audit logs and proof that logs include key usage and request traces. also encryption at rest and KMS integration.
[04:31] Carlos: we have SOC 2 + detailed audit logs, and KMS/HSM integrations for private deployments. we'll send the docs.
[04:38] Maya: any limits on number of project keys or rate-limiting rules? we're multi-team, expecting hundreds of keys.
[04:44] Priya: no practical limits; the console supports bulk key creation and templates. programmatically you can create keys in bulk via the API.
[04:55] [05:00] Maya: what's the failure mode? if a key exceeds a project quota, do requests fail with 429 or degrade to cheaper model?
[05:07] Priya: you can configure fallback policies - by default it returns 429, but you can set automatic fallbacks to a lower-cost model or route. for critical paths customers often set soft limits with alerts and hard limits with fallbacks.
[05:23] James: pricing - how do you bill per-org committed tokens vs per-key usage?
[05:28] Carlos: billing is at org level; project keys let you attribute usage to projects for internal chargeback. committed capacity discounts apply at org level. we'll send the SKU sheet.
[05:40] [05:40] Priya: quick note on implementation - the enforcement token bucket is distributed; we use local caches plus a central quota service. this keeps p99 latency low while still enforcing global quotas. there may be transient overcommit in large bursts but the burst token bucket handles that.
[05:59] Maya: any integration with our SSO? can keys be scoped to users/roles?
[06:05] Priya: yes, you can sync SSO groups and map them to projects and roles; keys can be bound to a service principal or user. we also support RBAC in the console.
[06:17] Lena: log retention - how long do you keep usage logs? we need 1 year plus export to our SIEM.
[06:24] Carlos: default retention is 90 days for hosted, with add-on options for longer retention and exports; private can be kept per your policy.
[06:34] [06:34] (Priya navigates to API docs)
[06:40] Priya: here's a sample cURL - show how header is returned and how to inspect X-Redwood-Quota-Remaining.
[06:48] James: good to have headroom programmatically.
[06:52] Maya: do you support per-customer (not per-project) spending caps? we'd like global account spend caps.
[06:58] Priya: yes org-level spend caps are supported with alerts and enforcement. if nearing cap we can pause non-critical projects or throttle them.
[07:12] [07:12] Lena: question about encryption keys - can we bring our own KMS for hosted?
[07:17] Carlos: for hosted we offer customer-managed keys for some plans; for Private you bring your own KMS/HSM. we'll surface exact options in the doc.
[07:26] James: curious about concurrent connections and burst TPS - what's the SLA?
[07:31] Priya: our hosted SLA covers uptime; latency SLOs depend on model and sequence length. for Dedicated we offer throughput SLAs per reserved GPU pool. we'll share numbers in the follow-up.
[07:45] Maya: any mention of competitors? we evaluated openai and anthropic; main differences were cost and deployment flexibility.
[07:52] Carlos: yep, deployment options and strong per-tenant controls are a differentiator.
[07:58] [08:00] (short wrap-up)
[08:02] Carlos: recap - we'll send pricing + SOC2 + KMS docs, provision trial org & project keys, and schedule the benchmark.
[08:10] Maya: thanks, that works.
[08:14] Priya: i'll follow up with the sample policy JSON and the benchmark repo link.
[08:20] Lena: we'll compile compliance Qs and send them over.
[08:25] Carlos: great, thanks everyone.

End of transcript.

Notes: transcription contains a few recognition errors (names and product terms sometimes mis-transcribed), see action items for owners.
